title: Van Westendorp Pricing Model: The Four Questions and What They Reveal
summary: The Van Westendorp pricing model returns four thresholds and an acceptable range. Learn when to use it and why the reasoning matters more than the intersection.
body_markdown:
What is the Van Westendorp pricing model? +


A price sensitivity method that identifies the range of prices consumers find acceptable, using four questions on where a price feels too cheap, a good value, expensive but tolerable, or too expensive. The four cumulative curves reveal an acceptable range and optimal price point, which you can use to set pricing guardrails before launch. It does not predict exact purchase volumes.


What is the optimal price point in Van Westendorp? +


The price where the fewest respondents describe the product as either too cheap or too expensive, sitting at the intersection of those two curves in the Van Westendorp model. It's a directional indicator, useful for testing whether a planned price falls within the range consumers find credible. It does not forecast demand.


What are the limitations of the Van Westendorp pricing model? +


The main limitations of the Van Westendorp methodology are that it evaluates a product in isolation, without competitive context, and can't estimate how many people will actually buy at a given price. Hypothetical answers inflate stated acceptable prices versus real behavior, and it performs poorly when consumers have no reference point for the category. Conjoint analysis is typically stronger for demand forecasting or trade-offs.


When should you use Van Westendorp versus conjoint analysis? +


Van Westendorp fits early, for a directional range on a defined concept. Conjoint fits later-stage decisions with competitive dynamics, multiple configurations, or demand modeling at specific price points. Many teams run Van Westendorp first, then conjoint to pressure-test prices against alternatives.


Can Van Westendorp be used for B2B pricing research? +


Yes, with more care around recruitment. B2B price sensitivity varies with budget cycle and procurement authority, so recruiting actual decision-makers with purchase authority is critical, and studies take longer to field since the target sample is harder to reach.


What is the difference between Van Westendorp and Gabor-Granger? +


The Van Westendorp method asks participants to name their own thresholds across four dimensions, producing a range and an optimal price point. Gabor-Granger presents specific price points and asks about purchase intent at each, generating a demand curve. Van Westendorp suits exploratory work with no price anchor; Gabor-Granger suits comparing intent across a shortlist of prices.
